Package com.bilt.pos.widget

Interface WidgetHost

public interface WidgetHost
What a Widget may use of the session that owns it, handed over in Widget.attach(WidgetHost). It is the widget's whole view of the session: a widget never holds the session itself, so it cannot ring the basket or move money, and everything it needs from the platform side — credentials, environment, a ready client — comes from here rather than from its own configuration.

Implemented by the session; integrators do not implement this.

  • Method Details

    • sessionId

      String sessionId()
      The identifier of the owning session, as ShopperSession.getSessionId() reports it.

    • credentials

      BiltCredentials credentials()
      The credentials the session was built with, or null when it has none. A widget that needs the platform checks platformClient() instead; this is for widgets that talk to the platform through a channel of their own.

    • environment

      BiltEnvironment environment()
      The platform deployment the session was built for; never null.

    • platformClient

      BiltPlatformClient platformClient()
      A client for the Bilt platform, authenticated with the session's credentials against its environment. Created by the session the first time a widget asks and shared by every widget of the session; the session closes it when it ends, so a widget must not. null when the session was built without credentials — a widget that cannot work without the platform throws from Widget.attach(WidgetHost) then, with a SessionError that says so.

    • operationExecutor

      Executor operationExecutor()
      The session's operation lane: the single thread its operations, and every observer callback, run on. Work submitted here runs in order with the session's own work and blocks it while it runs, so it suits short state updates that must be ordered with the callbacks, not anything that waits on the network or the screen.

    • callbackExecutor

      Executor callbackExecutor()
      Where the session delivers its handlers to the register — the builder's callbackExecutor, or an executor that runs on the calling thread when none was configured. A widget delivers its own register-facing callbacks here so they arrive the way the register configured for the session.

    • reportBackgroundError

      void reportBackgroundError(SessionError error)
      Reports a failure of the widget's background work — a decision request that failed, a surface that could not render — through the session's onBackgroundError handler, the one place a register hears about failures that have no result object to carry them. Fire-and-forget; never throws.

    • context

      SessionContextSnapshot context()
      The session's context as of now: phase, attributes and lane identifiers.
